To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) real estate plays a critical role in the transmission of shocks to the economy, and that this role is amplified when real estate markets become tighter; and (2) real estate plays an important role in the transmission mechanism, because it is used as collateral by firms, and it is the main asset that is subject to the real estate price cycle.

(1) real estate markets are an important transmission channel of bank flow shocks, (2) real estate markets amplify bank flow shocks, and (3) real estate markets do so by increasing credit supply to firms that are more dependent on real estate collateral.

bank flow shocks have a differential impact on output growth across cities, with the most real estate exposed cities growing more, and this is mainly driven by the differential response of real estate prices.
